A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same kernel-based offline reinforcement-learning work. Their main text, equations, displays, and complete Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching relocated assumptions and renumbered results.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, theoretical bounds, and proofs, including its appendices. Table 1 compares theoretical suboptimality bounds; no original experimental or simulation outcomes are reported.

after.justification: v2 Section 5 reports original simulation results for a custom MDP and Gym CartPole, displayed in Figures 1 and 2.

M1.justification: The method retains kernel ridge reward estimation, pessimistic reward relabeling, and kernel PEVI with horizon-based data splitting. Algorithm 1 is simplified, but splitting remains in Algorithm 3. The newly supplied kernel-trick expression documents computation rather than establishing a different procedure.

E1.justification: v2 introduces actual evaluation on a custom continuous-state MDP with wrapped transitions and on Gym CartPole. v1 contains only abstract MDP settings and theoretical analysis, so these establish the paper's empirical task coverage.

E2.justification: Section 5.2 and Figure 2 newly evaluate linear, quadratic, and cubic finite-dimensional feature representations against squared-exponential kernel features. v1 has no empirical comparators; its PEVI and PDS entries in Table 1 are theoretical comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 introduces policy-value evaluation using a squared-exponential kernel and dataset-size sweeps. Figure 1 uses labeled counts 10, 20, 50, and 100; Figure 2 uses 20, 50, 100, and 200, with unlabeled counts extending to 500. These are new experimental protocols, not revisions of earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Figure 1 newly examines sensitivity to labeled and unlabeled sample sizes and compares simulated values with fitted inverse-square-root scaling curves. Figure 2 examines feature-representation choices across sample sizes. v1 contains no corresponding empirical sensitivity or representation analyses.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 newly describes estimating the scaling curve's constants by linear regression on simulation results, adding a statistical fitting procedure. Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds all results in Figures 1–2: increasing toy-MDP values with more data and CartPole comparisons generally favoring kernel features, especially with scarce unlabeled data. Figure 2 also shows quadratic features exceeding the kernel at larger unlabeled counts when N1=20. No same-setting empirical results exist in v1.

T1.justification: The principal assumptions and bounds remain, with v1 Assumption 4.3 relocated as v2 Assumption 3.2. Appendix B corrects the polynomial exponent in v1 Equation (72)/v2 Equation (68) and replaces an unjustified equality with an inequality in Theorem B.4's proof. Table 1 also adds optimal-policy expectations to its information-quantity definitions.

C1.justification: The introduction adds explicit applicability claims concerning avoidance of uniform coverage and global coverage across policies. It also reframes data splitting as employing an existing technique. The central kernel-PDS extension, finite-horizon scope, and substantive abstract and conclusion claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the toy curve fit as support for the proposed asymptotic behavior and attributes CartPole advantages to more flexible approximation of rewards and dynamics. The existing warning that the coverage assumption fails for infinite-dimensional cases remains, now organized as Remark 4.9.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's mathematical pseudocode, v2 supplies a Python/NumPy implementation statement and a repository URL described as public. It documents the kernel computation, toy transition and reward formulas, alpha=3, C=H=8, modulo state handling, and polynomial feature constructions. Repository contents were not accessed.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds Uehara and Sun (2021), Yin et al. (2022b), Blanchet et al. (2024), and Hu et al. (2024), extending discussion to partial coverage, differentiable approximation, robust offline RL, and offline-to-online learning. The central positioning relative to PDS and PEVI remains.

P1.justification: v2 revises contribution bullets, removes a duplicated introductory sentence, adds kernel examples, and moves the Bellman-closure assumption into Background. It numbers related-work subsections and adds Experiments and Acknowledgments. Most existing exposition and the appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The new two-panel Figure 1 and four-panel Figure 2 introduce substantial empirical visualization absent from v1. Table 1 is retained with its caption moved above it and revised, while journal headers and algorithm formatting also change.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful illustrative experiments and implementation information to the previously theoretical paper, while correcting local mathematical errors. These improve support and inspectability, but the gains remain limited: the fitted toy curves do not establish the acknowledged unproved asymptotic rate, and the CartPole results lack run counts, uncertainty reporting, and several reproduction settings. The principal theoretical contribution is unchanged.
